training
allows YOLO9000 to predict detections for object classes
that don't have labelled detection data. We validate our
approach on the ImageNet detection task. YOLO9000 gets
19.7 mAP on the ImageNet detection validation set despite
only having detection data for 44 of the 200 classes. On the
156 classes not in COCO, YOLO9000 gets 16.0 mAP . But
YOLO can detect more than just 200 classes; it predicts de-
tections for more than 9000 different object categories. And
it still runs in real-time.

10 batches our network
randomly chooses a new image dimension size. Since our
model downsamples by a factor of 32, we pull from the
following multiples of 32: {320, 352,..., 608}. Thus the
smallest option is 320× 320 and the largest is 608× 608.
We resize the network to that dimension and continue train-
ing.
This regime forces the network to learn to predict well
across a variety of input dimensions. This means the same
network can predict detections at different resolutions. The
network runs faster at smaller sizes so YOLOv2 offers an
easy tradeoff between speed and accuracy.
At low resolutions YOLOv2 operates as a cheap, fairly
accurate detector. At 288× 288 it runs at more than 90 FPS
with mAP almost as good as Fast R-CNN. This makes it
ideal for smaller GPUs, high framerate video, or multiple
video streams.

Darknet-19. We propose a new classification model to
be used as the base of YOLOv2. Our model builds off of
prior work on network design as well as common knowl-
edge in the field. Similar to the VGG models we use mostly
3× 3 filters and double the number of channels after ev-
ery pooling step [17]. Following the work on Network in
Network (NIN) we use global average pooling to make pre-

is simultaneously detecting 9000 other object categories, all
in real-time.

geNet we see it learns new species of animals well but strug-

YOLO9000 Best and Worst Classes on ImageNet.
The classes with the highest and lowest AP from the 156 weakly
supervised classes. YOLO9000 learns good models for a variety of
animals but struggles with new classes like clothing or equipment.
New animals are easier to learn because the objectness pre-
dictions generalize well from the animals in COCO. Con-
versely, COCO does not have bounding box label for any
type of clothing, only for person, so YOLO9000 struggles to
model categories like "sunglasses" or "swimming trunks".

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline outcomes are measured on fixed external benchmark test sets (PASCAL VOC 2007/2012, COCO test-dev2015, ImageNet detection validation) using standard mAP and FPS protocols, with no reported optimization against those test labels.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard benchmark test-set ground-truth labels evaluated via mAP and FPS on PASCAL VOC, COCO, and ImageNet detection tasks.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Supervised training losses on COCO, VOC, and ImageNet classification data, including detection coordinate/objectness losses and classification loss.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding superior speed-accuracy trade-offs (e.g., 76.8 mAP at 67 FPS on VOC 2007) and cross-dataset weakly supervised detection (19.7 mAP overall on ImageNet detection validation) are directly corroborated by empirical results.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation is comprehensive across standard computer vision benchmarks including PASCAL VOC 2007, VOC 2012, MS COCO test-dev, and ImageNet detection challenge sets, including step-by-step ablation analyses of architectural components and explicit comparisons of runtime speed and mAP.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluations are conducted on standard benchmark test sets (PASCAL VOC 2007, VOC 2012 test server, COCO test-dev2015, and ImageNet detection validation) with fixed external protocols.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard benchmark test-set ground-truth labels evaluated via mean Average Precision (mAP) and frames-per-second throughput metrics.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Standard supervised multi-task loss functions (cross-entropy classification loss, coordinate regression loss, and IoU objectness loss) optimized via stochastic gradient descent.

primary.limitations: The authors identify specific failure modes and performance drops, noting that YOLO9000 struggles with object categories such as clothing and equipment where COCO lacks representative bounding box annotations.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing the Darknet-19 backbone, anchor box clustering via IoU distance metrics, coordinate constraint formulations, multi-scale training intervals, and the construction and loss propagation mechanisms of WordTree.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript offers substantial algorithmic and architectural contributions, clear technical descriptions, rigorous multi-benchmark evaluations with extensive ablations, and candid discussions of limitations.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces YOLOv2, an improved real-time object detection architecture incorporating anchor box dimension clustering, direct location prediction, fine-grained passthrough features, and multi-scale training, alongside YOLO9000, a joint training method combining detection and classification datasets via hierarchical WordTree representation to detect over 9000 object categories.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript offers substantial algorithmic and architectural contributions, clear technical descriptions, rigorous multi-benchmark evaluations with extensive ablations, and candid discussions of limitations.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors identify specific failure modes and performance drops, noting that YOLO9000 struggles with object categories such as clothing and equipment where COCO lacks representative bounding box annotations.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
